title: Naming the band: Alexander, Lawrence and Duhe, Nile
summary: The band is renamed as players leave and Herbert Hall joins; Lawrence trains boys who get picked up by Baton Rouge bands.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Dajon, Alexander. And at that time the band was named by him, Alexander Right Time Band. And after he got droned, then the way Cromont player and myself, we called it Lawrence and Dewey Arbster. So we played, well I don't remember how many years we played together. And he left the country, so we had another boy to play in his place. And we keep switching off, get some new mans until, then we, until this boy came in with us, Herbert Hall. Well he played the banjo and then after he switched to clarinet. And then we changed the band name again, we called it Nile Band. Called it which? Nile.

Well we just, we just called, we just gave it that name. Just made it up. Well the, the Tromont player, the young fellow, he said, well let's change the name. And he gave that name, I think it's an angel name or something like that. So we went by that name for a small good wife, and then the band began to change again. At that time I began to train boys to play. You see, the minute, well Clarence started to play with me, and the minute he could play good, the band from Baden-Rouge would pick him up. I learned to teach a boy to play trumpet. When he could play good, they picked him up. And the saxophone, two of them, they all left.
